## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ariyadhammavipākakathā* (Kv 7.9) is a debate located in the seventh chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The controversy examined in this section concerns the proposition that there is a maturation (*vipāka*) of noble phenomena or states (*ariyadhamma*) [Bareau 1955]. Proponents of this view argue that the "great fruit" (*mahāpphala*) constitutes the ascetic life (*sāmañña*) and the holy life (*brahmañña*), and maintain that the four spiritual fruits are indeed karmic maturations, being the fruits of giving (*dāna*), virtue (*sīla*), and mental cultivation (*bhāvanā*) [Bareau 1955]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions are identified by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse within the *Kathāvatthu* itself, identifying 277 matching passages shared across 22 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual alignments occur with the *Sāmaññaphalakathā* (Kv 19.3, particularly §4.14–5.16 with §3.7–5.3), *Parūpahārakathā* (Kv 2.1), *Aparāpisamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.9), *Aññāṇakathā* (Kv 2.2), and *Sīlaṁacetasikantikathā* (Kv 10.7) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring machine alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan fragments of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the Tibetan *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā*, and the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
